ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, point R is outside the circle on the left side, and two secants are drawn from R. The upper secant first intersects the circle at U, then intersects the circle at S; the lower secant first intersects the circle at T, then intersects the circle at Q. The arc SQ on the right side of the circle is labeled 103°, and the arc UT on the left side of the circle is labeled 43°. Reasoning: By the theorem for an angle formed by two secants outside a circle, the measure of the exterior angle is equal to half the difference of the measures of the two intercepted arcs. Therefore m∠R = 1/2(103° - 43°) = 1/2 × 60° = 30°.
